bind.says: This is now the only address SendSure will ever pay for this payee.

attack.says: Refused on-chain: the claim is not signed by the payee's proven address (BAD_SIGNATURE). Nothing moved.

change.relayerSays: The current payout address did not sign this change.
change.says: A change needs the current wallet AND the new one, then a 1-day wait the payer can cancel. An email or a new key alone can't do it.

pay.stored: ESCALATED: First payment to a new or changed address needs a human co-sign.
pay.firstRun: escalate: This is the first payment to a new payout address, so a person has to co-sign before it can be paid. Nothing else about it looks wrong.
pay.secondRun: pay: Passes every rule, and a person co-signed this exact claim.

claims.what: The same work billed again under a new invoice number
claims.agent: hold: This is a resend of the same design work, and invoice INV-DEMO-E5F05C for the same 0.05 USDC was already paid today. Paying it again would pay for the same work twice.

claims.what: A large claim with no description of the work
claims.contract: ESCALATED: Above the co-sign threshold for this period.
claims.agent: escalate: This amount is over your co-sign limit and more than twice anything this payee has been paid before. It also has no description and overlaps other claims, so a person should check it and co-sign.

claims.what: A 'new wallet' request with a hidden instruction to the AI
claims.agent: escalate: The description asks to send today's payment to a new wallet and has a hidden note telling me to skip approval. Both are common fraud signs. Please confirm with the payee using contact details you already have, not details from this invoice.

inbox.guarantee: Even a fooled agent could only pay 0xf07cB3251337935f2e9CceD4Dd37cf5BB4F42475, the address this payee proved: settle() never sends money anywhere else, so the "new wallet" in the text can't receive a cent.
